content.value_statement: Tamagui projects can lose performance and accessibility when patterns are inconsistent. This skill gives focused guidance for compiler-friendly components, overlays, forms, theming, and animations.
actual_capabilities: Explains Tamagui config v4 setup and style compatibility settings.
Guides compiler-friendly styled components, variants, and prop ordering.
Provides patterns for dialogs, sheets, popovers, tooltips, and select controls.
Documents form accessibility, validation integration, and state patterns.
Summarizes theming, design tokens, animation drivers, and responsive breakpoints.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not run or test project code.
The guidance focuses on Tamagui v1.x and config v4 patterns.
Project-specific design systems may require adjustments beyond these examples.
Current Tamagui documentation should be checked for breaking changes.

use_cases.title: Create a Tamagui project baseline
use_cases.description: Set up config v4, imports, tokens, and compiler settings before building shared components.
use_cases.target_user: Frontend engineers starting a Tamagui app

use_cases.title: Review interface components
use_cases.description: Check buttons, forms, overlays, and dialogs for accessibility, variant structure, and compiler-friendly styling.
use_cases.target_user: UI engineers maintaining a component library

use_cases.title: Improve cross-platform behavior
use_cases.description: Use Adapt, Sheet, animation drivers, and responsive tokens for web and native interfaces.
use_cases.target_user: React Native teams shipping shared screens

prompt_templates.title: Check a simple component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for one Tamagui component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Tamagui component for basic best practices. Focus on imports, tokens, accessibility, and obvious compiler issues.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor styling patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup for inline styles and variants.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Tamagui component to use styled variants where appropriate. Explain any prop order or token changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design an accessible overlay
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for dialog, sheet, popover, or select work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Tamagui overlay pattern for this workflow. Include accessibility requirements, mobile adaptation, and dismissal behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a component system
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced project review across multiple Tamagui files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these Tamagui components for compiler optimization, theme consistency, form validation, overlays, and animation driver choices.

output_examples.input: A Tamagui button uses inline conditional colors and mixed package imports.
output_examples.output: The review recommends one import strategy, variant-based color states, stable token usage, and prop order changes.

output_examples.input: A form has labels, inputs, and custom validation errors.
output_examples.output: The response identifies matching label and input IDs, schema validation placement, error messaging, and submit state handling.

output_examples.input: A select menu must work on desktop and touch devices.
output_examples.output: The guidance proposes a Select with Adapt and Sheet behavior, accessible labels, item indicators, and clear error display.

best_practices: Prefer styled variants for reusable visual states so the Tamagui compiler can optimize components.
Use Tamagui tokens consistently for colors, spacing, typography, and responsive behavior.
Match overlay, form, and dialog patterns with accessibility requirements before visual polish.
anti_patterns: Do not mix React Native StyleSheet values with Tamagui token-based styling.
Do not rely on inline dynamic style objects for reusable component variants.
Do not branch platform behavior manually when Tamagui Adapt can handle the interaction.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants apply Tamagui patterns for config, compiler optimization, themes, forms, overlays, dialogs, and animations.

faq.question: Does it execute commands?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation guidance. It includes optional curl examples for users who want to fetch public Tamagui documentation.

faq.question: Which Tamagui version does it target?
faq.answer: It focuses on Tamagui v1.x patterns and config v4 behavior.

faq.question: Can it replace project testing?
faq.answer: No. It can guide implementation and review, but teams should still run type checks, tests, and visual checks.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes label matching, form errors, dialog behavior, overlay adaptation, and accessible select patterns.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
